articles.headline: England star Kildunne dropped for Canada rematch
keyFacts: Head coach John Mitchell made four changes to England's starting XV, including dropping Ellie Kildunne to the bench, following a defeat to Canada that ended a 41-match unbeaten run.
Canada will host England in Ottawa this Friday for a rematch after Canada previously won 24-21 in Toronto last week and drew 26-26 in Exeter last month.
Mitchell said the team aims to respond on Friday by getting back to being hungry, accountable, and applying sustained pressure.
body: England's Red Roses: Ellie Kildunne benched as part of four changes to starting XV in search for victory in Canada rematch

Canada's women snapped world champion England’s 41-match unbeaten run with a 24-21 victory in Toronto last Friday; Last month, Canada also drew with England 26-26 in Exeter to halt the Red Roses' 39-Test winning run; Canada host England in Ottawa this Friday October 23
Wednesday 21 October 2026 14:09, UK
Ellie Kildunne has been dropped to the bench in the England Red Roses squad to face Canada on Friday, a week on from suffering defeat in Toronto which ended a 41-match unbeaten run.

Head coach John Mitchell has made four changes to the starting XV in total, with Gloucester-Hartpury duo Emma Sing and Mia Venner coming into the back three at full-back and wing respectively, while Helena Rowland of Loughborough Lightning returns at inside-centre.
In the forwards, there is just one amendment to the team that began the second Test - Sadia Kabeya, also of Loughborough Lightning, is selected at openside flanker.
While Kildunne - 2024's World Player of the Year - and back-row Alex Matthews move to the replacements bench, wing Claudia Moloney-MacDonald and centre Tatyana Heard drop out of the squad altogether.
"Friday is our first chance to respond," Mitchell said.

"Last Friday, we lost sight of what we could control when it mattered most; that's on us to fix. This week is about getting back to who we are: hungry, accountable to each other and demanding more of ourselves than anyone outside this group ever could.

"We've earned a strong period, but nothing about it is owed to us going forward. Friday is an opportunity to apply sustained pressure, learn from what we missed and come out the other side better than we went in."

articles.headline: Championship referees 2026/27: A whistle-stop tour
keyFacts: Pro Ref merged several previous groups into one Professional Referee Group for the 2026/27 season to give officials greater scheduling flexibility.
Championship clubs rejected the Football Video Support system for the 2026/27 season, meaning referees do not have VAR fallback options.
Stephen Martin issued the highest average of yellow cards per game at 4.75, while David Webb issued the lowest at 2.62 during the 2025/2026 season.
body: Getting some research done on Championship referees can really help when it comes to betting on the EFL this year. If you’ve got some context on an individual ref like cards shown or fouls/penalties given it can help you decide what would work best as part of an ACCA or even just a single bet.

The EFL Championship is the second-biggest league in England and with that comes a level of scrutiny beaten (arguably) only by the Premier League. As the second-most attended domestic league in the world, drawing well over 11 million spectators a season, there’s a lot of info that you can derive from a referee’s performance over a campaign.

You’ll want to know things like whether or not the appointed ref for a game has a tendency to book more than the average man in the middle, because it all forms the context of your potential football betting plan for the 2026/27 season.
A look at the current Championship referees

The pool of EFL Championship referees changed for the 2026/27 season, as Pro Ref merged the previous Select Group 1, Select Group 2 and Supplementary List into one Professional Referee Group. This group now mainly assigns officials for both the Championship and Premier League, giving Pro Ref greater flexibility when making appointments for specific games. National Group officials mainly work across League One, League Two and the National League.

There used to be a far more distinct difference between Premier League and Championship referee assignments, but this was designed by Pro Ref as a way to “both greater competition and flexibility to appoint and recognise high-performing match officials”(via the official EFL site ).

Even with those changes, it’s still worth looking at some of the busier referees from last season’s EFL Championship campaign, so you can get a gauge of what to expect when they’re appointed through the season.
Josh Smith
Referee Josh Smith took charge of 27 Championship games in the 2025/2026 season recording a rate of 96 yellow cards given and 6 red cards issued.

Smith was in the middle for the Steel City derby game at Bramall Lane during the 2025/26 season, where Sheffield United beat Sheffield Wednesday 2-1 back in February 2026. Derbies are always high-profile fixtures, and Smith gave out two red cards (one for each side) during the 90 minutes.

So far this season, Smith has taken charge of six Championship games and shown 30 yellows, with no reds. Nobody has shown more yellow cards in the second tier so far, with Tim Robinson and Ruebyn Ricardo next on 29 each. Smith also took charge of the top-of-the-table clash between Swansea and West Ham on 17 October.
David Webb

Referee David Webb was the main official for 26 EFL Championship games during the 2025/26 season, and he was a lot less eager to reach into his pocket than some colleagues. Webb gave out 69 yellow cards during the season as well as only 1 red.
That has remained the case this season, with Webb showing 10 yellow cards in four Championship games. He did not book a single player in Blackburn’s 1-0 win at Bristol City on 13 October.

He also handled the main officiating duties in the reverse Steel City derby at Hillsborough during the 25/26. Sheffield United won that game 3-0 in November 2025, with only 3 yellow cards given to Wednesday during the tie.
Anthony Backhouse

Referee Anthony Backhouse officiated 25 EFL Championship games during the 2025/26 as the main man in the middle. Backhouse was one of the busier Championship officials last season, as he dished out 116 yellow cards, but did not issue any reds.

Backhouse was in charge for the East Anglian derby at Carrow Road, where Ipswich were able to beat their Norfolk rivals Norwich 2-0. 5 cards were issued to the home side whilst the Tractor Boys got 6 on the day.
So far this season, Backhouse has refereed six Championship games and handed out 22 yellow cards (and 0 reds). That is an average of 3.67 per game, well down on last season’s 4.64.
Championship refereeing trends – at a glance

The table below includes all of the referees that handled at least 23 EFL Championship games during the 2025/2026 season and is ordered by yellow cards per game from the highest issued (Stephen Martin) to the lowest (David Webb).

The spread between the top and bottom is really wide, with Stephen Martin having issued an average of 4.75 yellows per game and David Webb only 2.62. Two other numbers jump out quite a bit, with Matt Donohue having given 7 penalties across 25 Championship games (producing a rate of 0.28 per game) and Lewis Smith having given out only 2 in 25 (at a rate of 0.08).
This season’s early leader on yellows per game is Ruebyn Ricardo, with 29 in five Championship matches (5.8 per game), the highest rate of any referee with four or more games.
Referee-related betting markets

Doing some research into the officials for a game makes a big difference to several betting markets, with disciplinary and foul-related prop bets being where the information you find will really show. Depending on which bookmaker and fixture you choose, the options I’ll outline below could be available as part of a bet builder or just individually.

Again, it’s all about figuring out the context. For example, if you look at Backhouse’s 4.64 yellow card average from last season and compare it to Webb’s 2.62, then you might take a different approach if one of them is the first official for a particular tie.
Yellow and red cards

Yellow card markets offer what is arguably the clearest reason to look closely at refereeing data. There’s a chance that you could find a ref that gives out more cards for specific games, more for a specific team or even individual players.

Whilst the 4.75 I’ve already referenced for Martin previously does not automatically mean that an over bet on cards issued is guaranteed, it feels like a relevant metric if both teams come in with big disciplinary numbers pre-match.
Reds are far more difficult to judge, because although a particular referee might’ve given out far more than a colleague, you don’t see the context of the game or the individual infractions.
Fouls

Foul markets aren’t as universally available at all sportsbooks, but some fixtures might offer specific players or match foul totals. How often the ref blows up to stop the game really matters here, as it gives you context as to how much they’re usually willing to let go during the course of the 90 minutes.

Looking again at the stats I provided earlier, Tom Nield averaged 23.13 fouls per Championship game in 2025/26, whereas Lewis Smith was at 19.4, so if one of those officials is in charge of a specific game (that you want to bet on), then you need to factor that in to decide on whether you bet on the over or under.
It’s all hypothetical of course based on last year’s stats, but it’s a good marker to know where you should probably be leaning.
Penalty to be awarded

Betting on penalty markets needs a bit more caution, as penalties actually being awarded during a football match is still pretty uncommon (despite what highlight packages might make you believe). 84 penalties were given across 552 Championship games during the 2025/26 season, which is equal to 0.15 per game (or roughly one penalty every 6.6 matches), so it’s not a frequent occurrence by any means.
How to find out who’s the ref before a Championship game

The EFL’s Match Officials page on the official EFL site is the best starting point to find information on referees. Batches of appointments are usually published before a gameweek, but there’s not a strict time that the EFL has to put this out every week. As an example of the timeframe, appointments for a mid-August round of fixtures were published three days before the first of those games kicked off.

Appointments for games are however not made at random. Pro Ref requires that officials submit an annual declaration of their interest. What that means is a referee cannot be appointed to a game where a club they support are playing or there is a recognised rival in the game of the club they support.

This policy also covers other factors, like previous involvement with an individual club, personal connections to individual players and potential geographical conflicts. Beyond that, appointments then need to consider potential issues such as practical, operational or performance factors.

Your best bet for a normal Saturday game is checking the EFL announcement list during the week. Club previews, established news outlets and some betting apps might then also have this information listed, but if it’s from the EFL site then you know it is 100% official.
FAQs about Championship referees
1. Championship games are often tight – how often are they decided by penalties or red cards?

Penalties and red cards make a huge difference during a game of football, but they do not decide every single game. As I’ve already mentioned, 84 penalties were given across 552 Championship games during the 2025/26 season, which is equal to 0.15 per game.
2. Is there any correlation between a higher number of fouls in a game to a lower number of goals?

The number of fouls in a game does not correlate to being a reliable standalone signal for fewer goals in a match. If the referee is blowing their whistle a lot then it will affect the rhythm of the game, but the amount of goals you can expect to see still relies on team quality, chances in front of goal and finishing quality of the players on the pitch.

You just need to look at the game between Wrexham and Sheffield United back in the 2025/26 season, which had Andrew Kitchen as the first official. Kitchen’s Championship matches averaged 20.1 fouls during the 25/26 season, but it was still a 5-3 win for Wrexham. There were 11 fouls given for that game.
3. Can a referee officiate multiple games for a specific team in one season?

Yes, as there is no rule that limits a referee to one league appointment involving a particular club during a season. What Pro Ref focuses on is eligibility and potential conflicts of interest before making appointments, so if someone has already refereed a team during that season, they’re likely to be eligible for another game.

David Webb is a clear example of this, as his 2025/26 games officiated included several Sheffield Wednesday matches, including games against Ipswich, Middlesbrough, Wrexham and the aforementioned Steel City derby against Sheffield United.
4. Do referees approach games differently in a league with no VAR?

The laws of the game aren’t changed because it’s an EFL Championship game, but the environment in which the decision-making takes place does change. Championship clubs rejected the proposed Football Video Support system for the 2026/2027 season, which means that the officials do not have a “fallback” when it comes to making decisions on the pitch, and everything the first official makes is final there and then.

This places a much greater immediate importance on the referee and assistant referees’ judgment during a game, but it also means that there won’t be as many stoppages to games as you’d find during a Premier League tie.

articles.headline: New PS5 Update Is Out Now, And Sony May Be Tightening Security Before GTA 6
keyFacts: Sony released PS5 Update Version 26.07-14.20.00 to improve system messages and screen usability.
The patch may address vulnerabilities exploited by homebrew users and hackers who recently released the Relapse exploit.
Sony may require the new update to run Grand Theft Auto 6, which releases on November 19.
body: Another day, another PS5 update, as Sony tweaks its system with another minor upgrade. It looks like business as usual for PS5 Update Version: 26.07-14.20.00, with Sony focusing on overall usage and message readability, but there are murmurs that the patch could also be quietly plugging a few jailbreak holes.
First, the actual update. "We've improved the messages and usability on some screens," Sony's succinct patch notes read.

For your average PS5 user, this won't mean much and downloading the new firmware is just part of the process before you can start playing a game. But people in the homebrew and PS5 jailbreaking scene will likely avoid an update just in case Sony fixes a vulnerability that pirates and modders have taken full advantage of. Recently, hackers released the "Relapse" exploit, which works on every PS5 firmware before the version 14.00.00 update that was released on September 16.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bd5-cvN7QX8

This meant most retail PS5s could be jailbroken to run pirated games, a nightmare scenario for Sony. With Grand Theft Auto 6 out on November 19, Sony will likely focus on further improving PS5 security as it enters an arms race against determined hackers. As users on the PS5 jailbreak subreddit have pointed out, Sony could make it mandatory for PS5s to be updated to version 14.20 to properly run the game.
In case you missed it, September's PS5 update was a pretty chunky one. It added a helpful new option for PS5 Pro owners, voice chat improvements, and tweaks to longstanding features.

articles.headline: Websites taken down across Europe ahead of critical cyber-security update
keyFacts: Two critical vulnerabilities have been identified in the PHP programming language, prompting the PHP Foundation to issue software updates on Wednesday.
Cyber-security agencies including the UK's NCSC urged organizations to apply the fixes immediately or take vulnerable systems offline to prevent hacker attacks.
Cloudflare chief technology officer Dane Knecht stated that early attacks are already emerging, and the NCSC advised organizations to monitor for security updates.
body: - Published
Organisations which rely on the PHP programming language are being told they should install a significant software update today - or consider taking their websites offline.
Two critical vulnerabilities with PHP, which is widely used across the internet, have been identified.
The PHP Foundation, which supports it, is issuing updates which address them on Wednesday afternoon.
The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes as soon as they become available.
The Netherlands' cyber-security agency says it is taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities identified.
The country's National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website.
Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible.
"Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note, external.
Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning, external.

"PHP is everywhere. It âquietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful â lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said.
Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers.
The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said.

"The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it.
He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold".
'Early attacks emerging'
The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution".
Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites.
Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was, external "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up".

The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP".
It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004.
PHP was created for web development. It is used on servers to implement what you see when you visit websites.
Not all websites use it, but it nonetheless powers a large portion of the internet.

articles.headline: The Brewers 'Timeless Ticket' issue with the World Series, explained
keyFacts: Fans who bought $1,000 Timeless Tickets in 2015 complained that the Milwaukee Brewers only offered standing room and 400-level seats for the World Series.
Brewers president of business operations Rick Schlesinger stated that the team erred on logistics and did not live up to the program's spirit.
The Brewers resolved the issue by allowing affected fans to keep their World Series tickets without losing their Timeless Ticket redemption for the future.
body: A quirky ticketing story has emerged from the awesomeness of the Milwaukee Brewers making it to the 2026 World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays : Back in 2015, the Brewers sold what was called a "Timeless Ticket" for $1,000.

That purchase got fans who bought it quite the perk: A ticket to any game, and that included postseason contests and the World Series. And in the fine print given to Timeless Ticket holders, it said that the Brewers would offer the "best available seat locations subject to ticket availability."
But some fans complained that they were offered standing room tickets, which doesn't seem like the best available seats.

Two Kenosha brothers who paid $1,000 each for a Milwaukee Brewers "Timeless Ticket" more than a decade ago say the team isn't fully honoring the promise that came with it — the chance to sit in the best available seats for a game as big as the World Series.

— TMJ4 News (@tmj4) October 20, 2026

More than a decade ago, lifelong Milwaukee Brewers fan Dustin Buck bought two "Timeless Tickets," hoping he'd one day get to watch his team compete in the World Series. Now, with the Brewers making their first appearance since 1982, he's finally getting that chance.
Buck was… pic.twitter.com/vuVc53YATg
— CBS News (@CBSNews) October 20, 2026 Brewers fans were not happy about the Timeless Ticket issues
From the Associated Press:
Danny Fochesato of Milwaukee bought a Timeless Ticket on his 27th birthday, planning all along to redeem it whenever the Brewers reached the World Series.

“Back in 2015, that was a big selling point from the sales people about this,” Fochesato said. “They really touted, ‘Hey, this is going to be the best available seats. You’re getting the priority just behind season ticket holders. Anything the season ticket holders don’t have, you’ll have dibs at it for the World Series.’ That’s kind of the story they sold.” ...

“We had a form, and it only had 400-level or standing-room options,” Fochesato said. “We couldn’t even know what game we had. We just had to put a preference of which ones we wanted, and then we had to submit the form and just sit and wait for them what we got. I immediately was like, ‘No, that’s bogus.’”
The Brewers responded to Timeless Ticket fan complaints
New: The Brewers say they “erred” on the logistics of fulfilling Timeless Ticket requests for World Series games, limiting fans to the 400 level and standing room tickets.
Those fans will now be able to keep those tickets AND retain their Timeless Ticket for a future game: pic.twitter.com/FvRSNyRVYA
— A.J. Bayatpour (@AJBayatpour) October 20, 2026 Here's what Brewers president of business operations Rick Schlesinger said:

"While we were able to accommodate all with seats, we received feedback from some that they were unhappy with their seat locations. Clearly, even with extraordinary limitations on available seats, we did not live up to the spirit of the program, and we have been working through a resolution."
How the Brewers resolved the Timeless Ticket issues
Update from the #Brewers on the Timeless Ticket situation. #MLB #WorldSeries pic.twitter.com/IwwmArFHTZ

— Emily Mae 🎤 (@emilymaeheller) October 21, 2026 Per a letter shared on social media by reporters, the decision was made to have those fans keep their World Series tickets that they got, but that they wouldn't count against the Timeless Ticket redemption.

articles.headline: Best Operator Traits in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
keyFacts: Players must collect undamaged Robot Cores from K9 units at the NuriGO Mall to power a Lab Door in Operation Shopping Hacks.
Destructoid stated that players must quickly loot the defeated K9 units before their self-destruction damages the required Battery Cores.
Destructoid reported that the Battery Cores have no practical use outside the mission and only sell for 200 DMZ Cash.
body: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ has some really cool missions to complete, and one of them involves powering a Lab Door with Robot Cores. You’ll come across this task during Operation Shopping Hacks, and you’ll need Cores that are in perfect conditions (damaged ones won’t work).
In this guide, I will briefly discuss how you can get more Robot Cores that works with the mission.
How to obtain Robot Cores in Modern Warfare 4

To find functional Robot Cores, the best spot is the NuriGO Mall located in the northeastern part of the map. I have marked the spot on the image above to make it easier for you. Go inside the fall, and you’ll find a station surrounded by K9 units. This is the best spot to find these mechanical dogs.

Remix by Destructoid via Activision Once you find a robot dog, kill it, and you’ll find the K9 Battery Core as a drop. However, you’ll need to be fast since the Robot Dog will explode once you kill it. If the explosion takes place, it will damage the Battery Core, making it unusable for the quest.
When it comes to killing the K9, that’s a rather easy task. I simply focused on the glowing spots in the back while keeping my distance. That’s the easiest way to kill the K9.

Once you have the four Battery Cores, follow the objective marker to reach the Lab Door. Then, you can use the Cores to power up the Lab Door and complete the objective. Aside from the mission, I haven’t found any practical use for these Battery Cores. They only pay 200 DMZ Cash, which is really low.

articles.headline: Bills have another player suspended by NFL for a spitting incident vs. Raiders
keyFacts: Buffalo Bills defensive backs Sam Franklin Jr. and Chauncey Gardner-Johnson were suspended one game by the NFL for spitting incidents against the Las Vegas Raiders.
ESPN and NFL Network reporters stated that Franklin denies the allegation and will appeal his suspension to try to avoid missing the Week 8 game.
If the suspensions hold, the Bills will be without both players when they face the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8 following their bye week.
body: The Buffalo Bills are coming off a big Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders and will now get a bye week to rest before returning to action in Week 8.

But for that Week 8 matchup, the Bills are going to be without a key defensive back, and not due to injury. Chauncey Gardner-Johnson was suspended by the NFL for a spitting incident during the Bills vs. Raiders game.

Somehow, he's not the only Bills DB to face this suspension from the NFL. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. is joining Gardner-Johnson on suspension for spitting in the Raiders game.
A second Bills DB suspended for spitting incident vs. Raiders
"Bills DB Sam Franklin Jr. was suspended one game today for unsportsmanlike conduct that the league said was a spitting incident vs. the Las Vegas Raiders," Schefter reports.
Franklin and Gardner-Johnson are two defensive backs now set to be suspended for the Bills' Week 8 game coming out of their Week 7 bye.
When the Bills face the Baltimore Ravens in Week 8, they're going to be down a few defensive backs if these suspensions from the NFL hold up.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo is reporting that Franklin "denies the allegation" that he spit toward or on someone during the Raiders game. Franklin will appeal the suspension and try to avoid missing Week 8's matchup.
If both are out for that matchup, Buffalo will have to roll with Damar Hamlin, Jalon Kilgore, and Cole Bishop as their main safety rotation, as Gardner-Johnson and Franklin both might miss that game.
It's a wild situation for the Bills to find themselves in, as two defensive backs are now suspended for Week 8, barring an appeal changing things.

articles.headline: Polymarket removes bets on outcome of Cornell sexual assault case
keyFacts: Polymarket removed a contract allowing users to bet on whether seven men accused of sexual assault would face felony charges.
More than $450,000 was wagered on the market before Polymarket removed it following public outcry, a company spokesperson said.
Advocacy group UltraViolet launched a petition urging celebrity endorsers like LeBron James to cut ties with the platform.
body: The online predictions market platform Polymarket has removed a contract that allowed users to bet on whether any of the seven men accused of sexually assaulting or exploiting will be charged with a felony sex crime.

More than $450,000 had been wagered on this question before it was taken off Polymarket's platform. It had been available since Sept. 30 and was slated to close on Jan. 31. The company's U.S. exchange is regulated by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which bans trading related to "activity that is unlawful under Federal or State law."

"Our primary goal at Polymarket is to bring objective, data-driven insight to the most important questions of our time," a Polymarket spokesperson said Tuesday. "This market addressed whether the government would take action — a process that deserves scrutiny, particularly in a case of such serious concern. That said, we believe in the wisdom of crowds, have heard them loud and clear, and removed the market."

Some of the recent outcry over the Polymarket contract has been aimed at its celebrity promoters. Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James has an endorsement deal with the platform, and he recently appeared in a star-studded commercial that also included cameos by Derek Jeter, Eli Manning, Sue Bird and several others.
A spokesman for Spike Lee, who also appeared in the Polymarket commercial with James, told the Associated Press the director had no comment.
Polymarket also has partnership agreements with the NHL, Major League Baseball, Major League Soccer, the UFC and ATP Tour.

A woman identified in court documents by the pseudonym Jane Doe last month that seven fraternity members sexually assaulted or exploited her in October 2024 and that Cornell mishandled her complaint. All of those men have denied her allegations, saying either that their interactions were consensual or that they weren't involved. They have not been charged with a crime.

Online critics characterized the Polymarket contract as degrading and questioned why celebrity ambassadors would associate themselves with the company. An online petition launched by UltraViolet, a women-led national advocacy organization, singled out James, Manning, Daddario and model Emily Ratajkowski while calling on other famous endorsers to cut ties with the company.

articles.headline: UK greenlights previously banned North Sea gas project sought by Trump
keyFacts: The UK government approved the Jackdaw North Sea gas drilling project, reversing a previous ban on regional fossil fuel drilling.
UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham faced pressure from Donald Trump and the fossil fuel industry to overturn the drilling ban.
Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said the Jackdaw project will begin supplying gas to homes and businesses by the end of the month.
body: The United Kingdom is allowing a proposed gas drilling project in the North Sea to move forward, a major reversal in the country’s climate change policy, which previously banned new fossil fuel drilling in the region.

The sign-off on the project, known as Jackdaw, had been expected for months, as new Prime Minister Andy Burnham faced intense pressure from the fossil fuel industry in the U.K. and from the Trump administration to overturn the North Sea drilling ban.

U.K. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh approved the project Wednesday, saying it would start supplying gas to homes and businesses by the end of the month. Fahnbulleh said the project moved forward in large part due to the country’s energy crisis, which she said has been triggered by the conflict in the Middle East and has reinforced efforts to expand domestic energy production.
Jackdaw is one of two major proposed drilling projects off the coast of Scotland that the fossil fuel industry has sought to move forward, the other being the Rosebank project.
In early 2025, the Court of Session in Edinburgh overturned license approvals for gasfield projects that were issued in 2022 and 2023.

At the time, the court said the approvals were unlawful and failed to fully assess the environmental impacts of the projects — such as the greenhouse gas emissions generated by the burning of oil and gas.

As part of the ruling, however, the court permitted the developers of the two projects, Shell and Equinor, to continue work such as drilling wells, as the government considered any future oil and gas production in the region.
Wednesday’s decision did not directly address the Rosebank license.
The legal challenges for the drilling projects coincided with the U.K.’s accelerated push to decarbonize and reduce the country’s reliance on fossil fuels.

The U.K. aims to hit net-zero emissions by 2050 and has moved to reduce fossil fuel development by lowering incentives and blocking future projects. In 2024, the Labour government committed to not permitting any new oil and gas drilling licenses in the North Sea.

The U.K. government also sought to suppress oil and gas development by increasing taxes on those profits from 35% to 38%, bringing the total tax rate for firms operating in the North Sea to around 78%, according to the Financial Times .
Fossil fuel lobbyists have said that increased oil and gas drilling will dramatically reduce the U.K.’s reliance on foreign sources of energy.
Since then, however, ministers have acknowledged that fossil fuel production will continue to play a critical role in supporting local energy demand.

In March 2025, Offshore Energies UK estimated that an additional 2 to 3 billion barrels of oil equivalent could be available in the North Sea by 2050. Any significant increase in oil production in the region could provide the U.K. with greater domestic reserves, as the nation looks to reduce its reliance on the Middle East.
And last summer, the U.K. government released new guidance related to environmental impact assessments for offshore oil and gas developers — and notably did not shun the fossil fuel industry.
Over the summer, Burnham also expressed an openness to approving more oil drilling in the North Sea, saying he planned to take a “pragmatic approach” regarding the region.
“When people are struggling, we can’t ignore that,” he said, according to Bloomberg .

The government’s decision Wednesday does hand a partial win to environmentalists and climate activists as it does not allow the issuing of new exploration licenses for drilling activities in the North Sea.
UK PRIME MINISTER HINTS AT APPROVING NORTH SEA DRILLING AFTER TRUMP PRESSURE
President Donald Trump has been pressuring the new U.K. government to do just that, claiming over the summer that Burnham told him that he would be opening up the North Sea entirely.

“If you use the North Sea, the U.K. will be a really rich country,” Trump said in July. “I cannot get the point across. The new gentleman, when I spoke to him, said he’s going to open up the North Sea.”

articles.headline: How Israel’s war on Lebanon has cost young people with autism and ADHD
keyFacts: The war in Lebanon has disrupted daily routines and caused sensory distress for young people with autism and ADHD, families reported.
Rising costs and specialist shortages have made neurodivergent therapy and education increasingly unaffordable for most families, experts said.
Lebanon is finalizing a national mental health strategy for children and teenagers to address support gaps, an official said.
body: Beirut, Lebanon – After her husband died from COVID-19 in 2020, Lena Kouyoumjian moved back to her parents’ house in Mazraat Yachouh, a village 20 minutes’ drive from Beirut. For Lena, energetic and outgoing, the move was difficult, but she accepted that she needed help to care for her 20-year-old daughter, Vana, who is autistic and non-verbal.
Lena first noticed her daughter’s symptoms when she was two years old. Vana is still unable to communicate verbally how she feels, but her mother does her best to understand her.
Like many autistic individuals – and neurodivergent people in general – Vana needs a supportive and stable environment, alongside a structured routine, to feel well.
Lebanon has been engulfed in war since October 2023, with bombings across the country and an economic crisis continuing to impact all Lebanese, particularly neurodivergent people.
When Israel escalated its attacks on southern Lebanon in March, as a trainer for children with disabilities, Lena understood that this could impact her autistic daughter.
“Any sudden change in routine, loud noises, fear, or uncertainty can increase their anxiety and make them feel unsafe,” Lena told Al Jazeera.
“I can see this in my daughter. Since the situation became more difficult, she has become more anxious and sensitive to the changes happening around her.”
Challenging a social stigma

The symptoms of autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) vary depending on the person and condition, but they frequently include sensory issues and emotional dysregulation. ADHD and autism often occur together, combining to make AuDHD, where traits from both conditions can be seen.
People with these neurodevelopmental conditions are often stigmatised by societies that do not fully understand them, including in Lebanon.

While the pressures caused by Israel’s war on Lebanon and mass displacement have led to psychological issues for many, neurodivergent people are more vulnerable due to their need for consistent support and routine.
“Being a parent of an autistic child isn’t something every parent can handle. A challenge I often face is deciding the amount of time and energy I should allocate to my child,” said Lena.

Lebanon’s Autism Awareness Association (AAA) has provided support for both mother and child. Vana has attended classes at AAA, a nonprofit based in Antelias, outside Beirut, for the past six years, which serves as an alternative school for young autistic people.

But rising costs in Lebanon during the war have prevented Vana from attending classes regularly. “Even transportation to her centre became very difficult, especially with the increasing financial challenges. At times, it became impossible for her to go, so she had to stay home,” Lena said.
Ghada Hayek Makhoul, who co-founded AAA with other parents of autistic children in 2015, said the group has made constant efforts to increase awareness about the condition in Lebanon.
“Many people don’t know what autism really is. They don’t know the spectrum; how it can vary from mild to moderate to severe,” Ghada told Al Jazeera.
Sensory overload

Ghada’s son, Anthony, is a calm 27-year-old autistic, non-verbal man who relies heavily on helpers. Although he is unable to speak, his mother said it is clear when he is distressed, putting his hands over his ears when he is in pain due to sensory discomfort.

Autistic people can be more sensitive to noises than neurotypical people. During the war, people in Lebanon have been subjected to a harrowing range of sounds, from Israeli bombs exploding on the ground to the sonic booms of warplanes flying overhead.
“So, imagine the drones all the time [for autistic people], the bombs, and the vibration of the bombs … all of this that we were hearing, so of course it affected him a lot,” Ghada said.
“My son can’t listen to the TV any more due to the news. He switches it off and removes the remote control. It’s too triggering for him.”
Anthony’s mother said he senses tension and anxiety, even if his understanding of what is being said or happening is limited.
“[It affects] all the senses, everything. He doesn’t want to go into a pool any more. He used to love the water. And now, he doesn’t want to go into the pool any more,” Ghada said.
“I don’t know what changed. Because it’s outside? Because of the sound? I don’t know.”
Mental health support as a luxury
Israel’s war on Lebanon has had a direct economic impact on the AAA and other organisations providing neurodivergent or psychological support.
Lebanon’s economic crisis, with inflation potentially reaching 17 percent this year, has also led to a brain drain of professionals who could support neurodivergent people.

AAA is a crucial support base for families with autistic children. But it comes at a significant cost of $700 per month for children attending five days a week. With 80 percent of the population living in poverty, few can afford such services.

“We need more trained staff, and we also need to keep the staff that are leaving the country. So, we need to have better salaries, but we cannot afford it, because we will have to increase the load on the parents,” said Ghada. “Things are in crisis mode for everybody during the war.”

The same thing is being seen with other mental health services. While many nongovernmental organisations (NGOs) provide free therapy, private consultations can cost more than $100 for a single 50-minute session.

Nour Toukan, a public health researcher at Enmaeya, a media platform focused on sustainable development, told Al Jazeera that care for people with autism or even for ADHD is “very much an out-of-pocket expense.”

While the government did launch a National Disability Allowance in 2023, with funding from the European Union and the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), the allowance of $40 per month is not enough to cover even the basics in Lebanon. People with autism can get a personal disability card, issued by the Ministry of Social Affairs, making them eligible for support, but those with ADHD cannot.
Lebanon’s National Mental Health Programme, established in 2014 by the Ministry of Public Health, is trying to bridge gaps in support caused by economic and geographic variables.
Dr Rabih El Chammay, the founder and director of the programme, told Al Jazeera a national mental health strategy for children and teenagers is being finalised.

“National studies addressing autism and ADHD have also been conducted, providing evidence to inform this work. We are meeting with several organisations, particularly organisations representing families of persons with autism, to understand priorities and build momentum for further coordinated action,” Dr Rabih said. “War makes this work more difficult because it can increase support needs while disrupting the services people depend on.”
Developmental regression
Displaced people have been the most impacted, but all of those in Lebanon whose schooling and routines have been disrupted are affected.

Adham Faraj, a 23-year-old psychology student at the Lebanese American University in Beirut, who was diagnosed with ADHD in 2024, said that when his classes moved online due to the war, he found himself staying at home more and more.
“It’s less engaging, especially if you struggle with attention. You’re less motivated to go out, so you just attend classes from bed,” Adham said.
Adham said the intensity of Israeli air strikes in Lebanon unsettled him, along with concerns about the rising price of medicine.
“There’s always a cheaper alternative, but it depends on people’s social class. Maybe an $11 box of medication is affordable for some, but not for everyone,” he said.

Rim Ajjour, a psychologist and psychotherapist in Beirut, whose work focuses on young people with autism, has seen that many of the skills neurodivergent people learned before the war are now being lost.
“With the limited resources available in Lebanon and the shift in people’s priorities, there has been more limited access to therapy,” she said.
Rim said that her clinic and others are doing their utmost to keep therapy accessible by freezing consultation fees, even when their own expenses are increasing.

With Israeli attacks continuing in southern Lebanon, which remains occupied by Israeli forces, in violation of a US-brokered June ceasefire, many fear the impact on their work in case of a return to full-scale war.
“I don’t know how we’ll be able to take it again,” Rim said.

body: A progressive congressional candidate backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he was detained by the Israeli military in the West Bank on Wednesday morning.

Brad Lander, a former member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), scored an upset primary victory this year against Rep. Dan Goldman, D-N.Y. But he was far from the New York City-area district this week, posting on X that he and others were being held by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) while on a trip to help Palestinian farmers harvest olives in disputed territory.

"I’ve been detained by the IDF, along with a group of rabbis & volunteers. We were simply harvesting olives in a grove near Nehalim in the West Bank. The occupation is a crime under international law. Harvesting olives isn’t a crime under any law I know," Lander posted on X.
LIBERAL MS NOW WRITER CALLS MAMDANI PRIMARY SWEEP A 'GENUINELY SCARY NIGHT FOR NEW YORK CITY JEWS'
Lander is one of several anti-establishment candidates who Mamdani backed in New York City Democratic primaries this year. And he's not the first to get into a dust-up with law enforcement, either.

Socialist candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier , who defeated Congressional Hispanic Caucus Chairman Adriano Espaillat, D-N.Y., in their primary race, said she was knocked to the ground by NYPD officers during a protest against federal immigration authorities shooting an illegal immigrant in the Bronx this month.
MAMDANI'S TEAM REPORTEDLY CLASHING WITH SOCIALIST CANDIDATE HE ENDORSED OVER ICE SHOOTING
Lander is the former New York City comptroller and a former member of the DSA . He left the organization in 2023 in response to a rally members held the day after the Oct. 7 attacks by Hamas .

The group he was with in the West Bank, Rabbis for Peace, posted a photo of Lander and said he was detained "by Israeli police for standing with Palestinians during the olive harvest" along with others.
FAR-LEFT SURGE: MAMDANI-BACKED CANDIDATES OUST DEM ESTABLISHMENT INCUMBENTS
"The Palestinians whose land this is have a right to harvest it in peace," Lander, who is Jewish, said in a video posted by the group.
It's not clear if Lander has been released or what the terms of his detention are. Fox News Digital reached out to his campaign and to Mamdani's office for comment.
New York's 10th Congressional District is overwhelmingly Democratic, meaning he is all but assured to win his general election and come to Congress next year.

articles.headline: Konami Has Staged the Biggest Unlikely Gaming Comeback of 2026
keyFacts: Konami has staged an unlikely gaming comeback by reviving dormant franchises like Silent Hill and Castlevania.
The publisher achieved this success by partnering with external studios to create smaller, tightly scoped games instead of massive blockbusters.
Recent releases like Silent Hill 2, Silent Hill f, and Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse have sold millions of units and revitalized the company's relevancy.
body: You don’t have to look very hard to find stories about publishers struggling to make ends meet in 2026. Skyrocketing budgets caused by a demand for franchise games to grow bigger and better with every installment have put major players like Sony and Microsoft in a tough spot. But in a sea of business horror stories, one small triumph is starting to emerge in the most unlikely of places: Konami.

After a decade of behind-the-scenes drama that turned a once-powerful publisher into a Pachinko punchline, Konami has begun to rediscover its footing in a real way. A successful Silent Hill 2 remake, quickly followed by the critically acclaimed Silent Hill f, revived an all-but-dead franchise in one year flat, to the tune of millions of units shipped. That strategy has only expanded in 2026, as the double whammy of Silent Hill: Townfall and Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse have proved that Konami has finally cracked the code to restoring the relevancy of its once-great franchises.

While it’s hard to make the same trick work across the board in the video game industry, other publishers may want to take note. Konami is currently laying out a potential vision for an industry that can find success by scaling back instead of going as big as possible.

It’s surprising that this is coming from Konami, considering that the publisher was on the brink of irrelevancy just a decade ago. The publisher’s now infamous fallout with Metal Gear Solid creator Hideo Kojima crushed good will from players and stalled any momentum it might have had coming out of its award-winning Metal Gear Solid 5: The Phantom Pain. While Konami didn’t stop making games altogether, its output from 2016 to 2024 wasn’t exactly impressive. Major franchises like Metal Gear Solid, Castlevania, and Silent Hill seemed to go dead as sports games and retro rereleases filled in the gaps.

Konami began to show some signs of life in 2023, when the publisher released Super Bomberman R 2 and Metal Gear Solid Master Collection Vol. 1, but the real sea change came in 2024. Seemingly out of nowhere, Konami revealed its intention to revive Silent Hill, starting with a quick experimental game called Silent Hill: The Short Message. Though it was a critical dud, it doubled as a proof of concept, and Konami made good on its plans later that year with a successful remake of Silent Hill 2. That project wasn’t handled by an internal team at Konami, but by Bloober Team, an indie horror studio that had made a name for itself over the past few years.

Two years later, it’s becoming clear that Silent Hill 2 was the start of an even grander strategy. 2025 gave us Silent Hill f, a follow-up helmed by NeoBards Entertainment, a developer who had a history of working with Capcom on games like Resident Evil: Resistance. With Konami’s support and free creative reign over a big IP, NeoBards delivered a radical reimagining of Silent Hill that resonated with fans. What could have been a risky gamble paid off, with the game selling two million units within six months of its release.

From that vantage point, it looks like Konami has cracked a clear strategy: Give the keys to its IP to proven external partners who can make successful installments in a limited scope. You can see that again this year in Silent Hill: Townfall, a very compact Silent Hill game created by Stories Untold developer Screen Burn Interactive. While we’ve yet to get a sense of whether it was a sales success for Konami, the fact that it’s a seemingly smaller scale production gives the publisher much more flexibility than an all-chips-on-the-table production would have.

Now, we’re starting to see that thinking extend to other Konami franchises. This month, Konami published Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, the first original game in the series in over a decade. Development duties were handled by Evil Empire, a small studio that cut its teeth working on Dead Cells and The Rogue Prince of Persia, both of which displayed obvious Castlevania inspirations. Rather than going grand, Evil Empire delivered a tidy 2D action game that has hit with Castlevania fans who were happy to get another classic Metroidvania rather than a major escalation of the franchise.

You can already see a path forward for Konami if it wants to push that momentum even further. Why not give the Castlevania keys to Ender Magnolia developers Adglobe and Live Wire next? Or how about commissioning Team Ladybug, a developer that has proven itself with retro action games like Blade Chimera, to make an even smaller-scale ode to Castlevania’s origins? The future suddenly feels wide open now that there’s not a feeling that every Castlevania game needs to be bigger and more expensive than the last. Maybe it finally makes dollars and cents to wind the clock back and make tentpole games compact again, leaning on smaller developers who know how to deliver a tightly scoped game.

Konami is ahead of the curve with its thinking, but there are signs that other publishers are warming up to that — with mixed success. Sony took a stab at it earlier this year with God of War: Sons of Sparta, a 2D prequel handled by indie developer Mega Cat Studios. It didn’t exactly land to the warmest reception, which might have left Sony with cold feet, but it’s hard to imagine that it’s as costly an error as a game like, say, Concord. Ubisoft and Sega have dipped into that trend too with Prince of Persia and Shinobi, respectively. Suddenly, it feels like franchises that have either fallen by the wayside or only get a new entry once every five or six years are getting more chances for creative reinvention.

Whether that works will no doubt come down to a case by case basis. Konami is currently knocking it out of the park because it keeps pairing the right franchises with the right third-party partners. The games feel scoped around what those studios can realistically deliver rather than matched to the expectation of a mega-budget success. Maybe there’s hope yet that the video game industry can rein itself in and find a sustainable way to keep franchise games alive.

articles.headline: Heat pump tech is 170 years old. Pascal thinks it’s time for an update.
keyFacts: Startup Pascal raised 8.5 million dollars in funding to develop more efficient refrigerators and heat pumps using new solid-state cooling materials.
CEO Adam Slavney said appliances using Pascal technology will be about 20 percent more efficient than existing models and avoid harmful greenhouse gases.
Pascal signed a customer contract for a pilot project, plans to deliver its first prototype early next year, and aims to release commercial refrigerators in 2028.
body: When the experimental results came back, they puzzled Adam Slavney and Jinyoung Seo. They had been testing a new class of materials for more efficient refrigerators, air conditioners, and heat pumps, a mission that the cooling appliance industry has been on for eons. The measurements for the materials that the team was testing shouldn’t have been different, but they were.
“Why are these things different? What did we change?” Slavney told TechCrunch. “We had an inkling of it within three-ish months, but we didn’t have definitive proof for a year or two.”

That proof is now underpinning Slavney’s startup, Pascal, where he’s co-founder and CEO and Seo is co-founder and CTO. The company recently raised $8.5 million in a follow-on to its seed round, co-led by Sazze Partners and LB Investment with participation from KDB Silicon Valley, the company exclusively told TechCrunch.

A refrigerator or heat pump using Pascal’s material promises to be around 20% more efficient than existing models, he said. (Both heat pumps and refrigerators use the same basic technology.) The startup has signed a contract with a multinational beverage company for a pilot of the technology.

“This whole funding round came together originally because we got a customer contract earlier than we were expecting to,” Slavney said. Pascal is on track to deliver its first prototype early next year, and it hopes to follow that with a batch of more polished refrigerators in 2028.

Scientists have been searching for better refrigerants for almost as long as refrigerators have existed. More recently, they’ve been looking for compounds that don’t harm the atmosphere in one way or another. They exist, but they also need to be at least as effective as existing refrigerants.

“We’ve been playing whack-a-mole with refrigerants for 35 years, 40 years,” Slavney said. Older gaseous refrigerants like Freon ate a hole in the ozone layer, while newer ones like R-134a are still extremely potent greenhouse gases. “It’s just a never-ending treadmill,” he said.

One alternative that has attracted researchers’ attention is a class of materials known as solid-state refrigerants. Because they’re solid, they can’t escape to the atmosphere, eliminating the climate and ozone concerns that haunt modern refrigerants. Solid-state refrigerants promise to make refrigerators and heat pumps more efficient. They work similarly to traditional refrigerants, giving off heat when squeezed and absorb it when that pressure is released.

Before his serendipitous discovery, Slavney and his colleagues at Harvard University had been researching the materials. “We wanted to do some high-pressure measurements, and the instrument that we were using required us to use gas. So we used the gas and then we swapped to a different gas and we were like, why are these different?” Slavney said.

After numerous additional experiments, the team realized they had discovered another path toward solid-state refrigeration. Rather than squeeze a solid block of material, Pascal’s heat pumps compress a gas — carbon dioxide — into a cartridge that contains a sponge-like material, which Slavney said is proprietary.

As the carbon dioxide works its way into the porous material, the gas molecules inside the pores start bouncing off the walls. Those collisions transfer energy to the material, warming it up. A heat exchanger then exhausts some of that heat. Run it in reverse and the material absorbs energy from the heat exchanger and transfers it to the carbon dioxide molecules.

In a Pascal refrigerator, two cartridges are running at any given time. One is absorbing heat from the inside of the refrigerator, transferring it to the carbon dioxide, while the other takes the heat from the carbon dioxide and transfers it to the outside air. Eventually, the cartridges become too hot and too cold, so the flow gets reversed.
“The material is very robust,” Slavney said. “We’ve cycled it up to 300,000 times. It’s the equivalent of a year or so in operation.”
The entire system moves heat more effectively than other solid-state refrigerants, which means that Pascal doesn’t have to operate at high pressures like other solid-state refrigerants might demand.
“We’re using conventional systems to do it,” Slavney said. “That mean we believe we can make it cheap, and that means we can make it widespread.”

articles.headline: 80 Israelis and Americans, including NY Democrat Brad Lander, detained in West Bank
keyFacts: Israeli security forces detained roughly 80 American and Israeli activists, including U.S. congressional nominee Brad Lander, in the West Bank.
The group was helping Palestinian families harvest olives when Israeli forces declared the area a closed military zone.
Israeli forces transported the detained activists to a police station for questioning.
body: 80 Israelis and Americans, including NY Democrat Brad Lander, detained in West Bank

NAHALIN, West Bank, and TEL AVIV, Israel — U.S. Democratic congressional nominee Brad Lander was detained along with about 80 American and Israeli rabbis and activists detained by Israeli security forces as they helped Palestinians harvest olives from their grove close to a settlement in the occupied West Bank.

This is the largest mass detention of activists in the occupied West Bank in at least a decade, two Israeli lawyers who work on these cases told NPR. And Rabbi Arik Asherman, a longtime Israeli human rights proponent, called the detentions "unprecedented."
It was not clear what they accused the group accused of by Israeli authorities. Israel's military and police did not immediately comment. The military had said the area was a closed military zone.

"We've been detained by the Israeli military for harvesting olives, and let's be clear: Occupation is a crime under international law," Lander said in a video he filmed from the bus the group was loaded onto to be taken to the police station. "Harvesting olives is not a crime under any law."

American rabbis from the U.S. organization T'ruah, the Israeli group Rabbis for Human Rights and other activists had joined Palestinian families in picking olives at their grove close to the Israeli settlement of Betar Illit.

Olive harvesting is an important time for Palestinians both culturally and economically. But it has become increasingly hard for Palestinians in the occupied West Bank to access their fields. Several Palestinians there told NPR they have been unable to harvest their olive trees there since the Hamas-led attack on Israel on Oct. 7, 2023, saying it had become too dangerous in the face of rising settler attacks in the occupied West Bank.

Wednesday's detentions came less than a week after American photojournalist Heidi Levine, working for The Washington Post was assaulted by Israeli settlers in the West Bank, the latest journalist to come under attack during the Palestinian olive harvest season.
Democratic congressman Ro Khanna of California was also briefly detained by Israeli forces during his trip to the West Bank in July.
The group of Americans and Israelis had joined the Palestinian farmers hoping their presence would help them harvest in peace.

After roughly two hours, drones began circling overhead and Israeli security forces arrived and declared the area a closed military zone. They detained the Israeli and American activists and took them to the police station for questioning.
This is a developing news story that will be updated.

articles.headline: OneDrive gives Macs a million things to keep in sync
keyFacts: Microsoft announced it is raising OneDrive's supported macOS sync limit to one million items to match Windows.
Microsoft stated that the macOS preview is scheduled for the Insiders ring this month, with general availability targeted for June 2027.
Microsoft added new features including Copilot analysis capabilities, Hero Links for managing permissions, and an admin command-line tool.
body: Microsoft is raising OneDrive's supported macOS sync limit to one million items, matching Windows, alongside new Copilot features, sharing controls, and an admin command-line tool.

The macOS preview is scheduled for the Insiders ring this month, with general availability targeted for June 2027. Eligible devices must meet hardware and configuration requirements; others retain the existing 300,000-item supported limit.
"This increase is intended to help organizations with large OneDrive and SharePoint libraries sync more content reliably across devices," Microsoft said.

However, sync performance may suffer for large numbers of read-only files or accounts under legal hold. "We are actively working to improve performance and reliability for these scenarios," Microsoft said.
Microsoft's cull of OneDrive's File Explorer shortcuts wasn't a retreat from AI. Its latest announcement gives Copilot more to do.

The assistant can now be asked to analyze across files (for example, selecting several spreadsheets and getting the bot to come up with charts and graphs), told to organize folders, or save a repeated workflow as a personal skill in a Markdown file. There is also a Prompt Gallery to save the user from having to come up with their own ideas.

Perhaps most interesting is the addition of "Hero Links," designed to end the proliferation of links to files and folders in OneDrive as permission needs change. The feature provides one link per file and folder by default, with permissions that can be updated while keeping the same URL.
Automatic expiration controls are still coming, however. Organizations that require time-limited access will want to check that gap before adopting the feature.

Administrators also get a OneDrive Sync command-line tool, available in private preview, for inspecting accounts, configuration, policies, and sync status. The tool can pull information from the OneDrive sync client and provide data on status, policy troubleshooting, and issue diagnosis, from folder backup and policy problems on a single PC to identifying devices that need attention across an organization.
And yes, there is, of course, integration with AI agents. ®

articles.headline: Australian politician struck by car in violent attack loses both legs
keyFacts: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines lost both legs after a driver allegedly struck her with an SUV twice in an attack.
Suspect Brendan Nugent appeared in court to face charges including intentionally causing serious injury and was remanded in custody until February.
The incident prompted senior opposition lawmaker James Paterson to call for a review of security arrangements for Australian politicians.
body: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines had both legs amputated after a driver allegedly struck her with an SUV twice in what authorities are investigating as a serious act of violence against a federal official.

Haines, 65, remained in critical condition Wednesday at a Melbourne hospital, where doctors amputated her right leg after initially removing her left leg following Monday’s attack in her hometown of Wangaratta. Her husband, speaking publicly for the first time since the incident, said she was alive and stable.
“The good news in all this is that Helen is alive and she’s stable. That is the most important thing for our family,” he told reporters in Melbourne.
“We are grateful and thankful that at this stage, both her heart and her mind are in good shape,” he added.
The attack has prompted calls for a review of security arrangements for Australian lawmakers as investigators work to establish a motive.
Tributes and flowers are placed outside the electoral office for independent member of parliament Helen Haines in Wangaratta, Australia, Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026. (James Ross/AAPImage via AP)

Brendan Nugent, 43, of nearby Tarrawingee, appeared in the Wangaratta Magistrates’ Court on Wednesday to face charges of intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury, and causing harm to a federal official.
Nugent did not enter a plea or apply for bail. He will remain in custody until his next court appearance in February. Police have not established a motive for the alleged attack.
According to witnesses, the driver rammed Haines with a Toyota Land Cruiser SUV, pinning her against her own vehicle before reversing and striking her again.

Nugent’s lawyer, Chirag Patel, told Magistrate Allison Vaughan that his client may be experiencing mental health problems but had never received a mental health diagnosis. Patel also said Nugent had idiopathic transverse myelitis, a rare neurological condition that causes inflammation of the spinal cord, as well as a concussion. The lawyer did not explain how Nugent sustained the concussion.
The alleged attack has raised concerns about the risks faced by elected officials who maintain close contact with their constituents.

James Paterson, a senior opposition lawmaker, called Wednesday for a review of lawmakers’ personal security, warning that attacks of this nature could threaten the accessibility that has long characterized Australian politics.

“The reality is that Australian parliamentarians by global standards are uniquely accessible to the public and that’s a good thing,” Paterson told the Australian Broadcasting Corp.

“But we … can’t have a situation where shocking attacks like this take place because that will fundamentally change our democracy forever if it becomes a serious risk to your life to be a member of parliament,” he added.

articles.headline: COD: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ players are spawning in the middle of a road and being flattened before they can do anything
keyFacts: Infinity Ward released early access for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ extraction mode, allowing pre-order players to test the game.
Players reported a bug where a spawn location on a road caused enemy AI patrols to instantly run them over upon entering the map.
Infinity Ward released a patch fixing instances where enemy AI could run over players while infilling.
body: Infinity Ward opened up early access to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ extraction mode overnight, meaning anyone who has pre-ordered a copy can now play the game's campaign as well as DMZ. And while early reactions to DMZ are fairly positive, there's one issue in particular, which a number of players have experienced, that has the capability of ending a round as soon as it begins.

The issue is to do with where DMZ spawns players. As an extraction shooter, DMZ's Hajin map offers multiple random spawn locations, and unlike traditional multiplayer modes, DMZ spawns are often on the edges of the map - far away enough from any action to allow players a chance to strategise and pick a target destination.

But unfortunately, one of the spawn-points Infinity Ward picked happens to be placed in the middle of a road, meaning that if you're unlucky, you might spawn as an enemy patrol is driving on it, flattening you and ending your round.

This nearly happened to Reddit user grillimperator, who was given a small window of time to jump out of the way. Reddit user Deep-Operation-3552, however, wasn't so lucky, immediately falling to the ground as soon as they got control of their character after the infil cutscene. As others noted in the replies, the timing of the 'Welcome to the DMZ' voice alert playing just as they die makes it all the more absurd. Judging by those examples, at least, there doesn't appear to be any form of spawn protection.

DMZ offers certain options to get back up after being downed, but if you don't have the necessary equipment, there's nothing you can do. Still, that wouldn't have mattered in the above instances, because the players were run over twice.
Given the persistent nature of DMZ, dying also means losing everything you entered the match with, which could be infuriating if that was the round you decided to pack your good gear.

Thankfully, the bug is one of several issues Infinity Ward fixed in a new DMZ patch. The patch notes specifically called out the problem: "Fixed some instances where enemy AI could run over players while infilling."

Modern Warfare 4's final mode, traditional multiplayer, unlocks at the game's full launch this Friday, 23rd October on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S and Switch 2. So far, players appear to be happy with the game's campaign, making it of the most well-received COD games on Steam. One player even managed to finish the campaign on its hardest, single-life mode YOLO.

articles.headline: Thousands of California public employees set to strike over contract
keyFacts: Thousands of California state workers prepared to strike on Wednesday after contract negotiations with Governor Gavin Newsom's administration reached an impasse.
SEIU Local 1000, representing roughly 100,000 public employees, is seeking a 20% salary increase, flexible telework, and higher healthcare contributions.
According to the union, roughly 5,000 essential workers determined by the labor board will report to work during the strike.
body: Thousands of California state workers were set to strike on Wednesday, rallying outside government buildings in several cities, as tensions boiled over lapsed contract negotiations with Governor Gavin Newsom’s administration.
SEIU Local 1000, a union that represents roughly 100,000 public employees, including nurses and teachers, has been pushing for higher wages, flexible telework and affordable healthcare.
The union has been at an impasse with the state since its contract expired on 30 June.

SEIU Local 1000’s negotiators say state officials rejected their key proposals: a 20% salary increase over three years, higher state healthcare contributions and flexible telework – Newsom has required state workers to be in office four days a week.

Union representatives also argued in a complaint filed with California’s public employment relations board that the state engaged in bad faith bargaining, by allegedly waiting until 30 June to respond to some of the proposals and saying there was “no money” for additional compensation.
The state has not commented publicly on the status of the contract negotiations, citing confidentiality.
A spokesperson for Newsom’s office did not immediately comment on the work stoppage.
Wednesday’s picketing marked a first for the union.

California’s department of human resources (CalHR) had reportedly attempted to block the strike, arguing the union did not have plans to exempt essential workers and thus was compromising public health and safety. The labor board determined a list of about 5,000 workers deemed essential, according to the union, who will report to work during the strike.

Manager Mike Ofo and promoter Frank Warren stated that Wardley can return to world title contention after taking a rest and recovery period.
Frank Warren said that if Wardley continues boxing, he will likely have a warm-up fight before pursuing another title.
body: Fabio Wardley offered route back to world title after 'rest and recovery' - 'We'll see where we go. He's a dangerous man'

Promoter Frank Warren believes Fabio Wardley can return to world title contention if the former WBO heavyweight champion chooses to continue boxing; Wardley lost a second consecutive bout to Daniel Dubois on Saturday when the Londoner beat him in two rounds at the O2 Arena
Wednesday 21 October 2026 13:51, UK
Fabio Wardley will be offered a route back to another world heavyweight title fight after his rematch defeat to Daniel Dubois.
Wardley was unable to regain the WBO world title after he was stopped in the second round of his second fight with Dubois at The O2 on Saturday.
But his manager Mike Ofo firmly believes that Wardley can challenge one of the other world champions after a "well-earned rest".

Oleksandr Usyk's decision to vacate his world titles has opened up new opportunities as Murat Gassiev holds a WBA title, while Agit Kabayel is the WBC champion, and Filip Hrgovic holds the IBF belt.

"You've got to look at some of the wins he's had. He beat Joe Parker, who was ranked No 1 in the world and everyone was saying, 'When is he going to get his shot at a world title?'
